description: When the hate online is loud and the accusations are flying, David shows us what to do. Not clapbacks. Not receipts. Integrity and honesty.
excerpt: He does not fight back with words. He does not try to prove them wrong. He turns his face toward God and asks Him to handle it.
verse: "See how many enemies I have and how viciously they hate me! Protect me! Rescue my life from them! Do not let me be disgraced, for in you I take refuge. May integrity and honesty protect me, for I put my hope in you."
body_html:
I wonder if this was a hard social media day when I highlighted these verses.

Being the Co-CEO of GiveSendGo, there are days when the hate online is loud. Really loud. Vicious in the way David describes here. Coming from every direction. Saying things that are not true. Attacking my character. Attacking the mission. Attacking me personally.

Days when it feels like everyone hates me.

They can be brutal.

And I wonder if that is why I highlighted these verses. Because David felt it too. Not the online part. But the vicious hatred part. He knew what it was like to look around and feel outnumbered by people who wanted him gone.

But watch how quickly he shifts.

He names the reality. See how many enemies I have. He does not pretend it is not there. He does not put on a brave face and act like it does not sting.

Then he goes straight to God.

Protect me. Rescue my life from them. Do not let me be disgraced.

He does not fight back with words. He does not try to prove them wrong. He does not go on the counter attack. He turns his face toward God and asks Him to handle it.

And then he says something I think is beautiful.

May integrity and honesty protect me.

Not clapbacks. Not receipts. Not sharper arguments. Integrity and honesty.

He is saying God, if I just keep walking with You, if I just keep doing what is right, that itself will be my protection. Because a life of integrity does not need to defend itself the way a life without it does. The truth stands on its own over time. The character speaks louder than the accusations. God is the one who vindicates.

That is such a good reminder for anyone who has ever felt piled on.

You do not have to answer every voice. You do not have to correct every lie. You do not have to prove yourself to every person who wants to see you fail. You just have to keep walking with God, keep being who you are, keep letting integrity and honesty be your posture.

And let Him handle the rest.

I want the hard days to actually mean something.

Because if I let it, criticism can grow me. Attacks can teach me things. Hard seasons can carve away the parts of me that were not really from God to begin with.

That does not mean I have to enjoy the hate. It just means I do not have to waste it.

And no matter what anyone says about me on any given day, God is still working. He is still shaping me. He is still finishing what He started in me. And the noise of the internet does not get to interrupt that.

I do not want to be distracted.

Not by the loudest voices. Not by the meanest voices. Not by the number of people who dislike me on a given day. Not by the accusations. Not by the drama.

That is who I am running to when the arrows are flying.
question: Where in your life are the loudest voices distracting you from the work God is doing in you?
